build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

comments.text: INIT, the module the linker runs first after BOOT ($6E11 = 3; its JSR is at $2BB5). Loads MDRIVER (load_init_file 8), and when the player kept the fast loader ($6DE5 = 0) its drive half, PIC64, into slot 5 before install_fast_loader, setting $6D9F to 1. Then CHARSET, which copy_block puts at $D000, and the title (title_screen). After the title it blanks the screens, prints the credits, loads SOUNDFX over MDRIVER, clears the game's memory and sets its starting values, loads the files every module needs, gives the party slots their default combat icon and offers PLAY GAME or DEMO.
CHARSET (file 2) at $6500; copy_block copies its 512 bytes to $D000 under the I/O area, the text screen's characters $00-$3F.
The title (title_screen), which returns at a key or when the tune has ended.

Black border and background and red frames ($6E35 = 2); clears the text screen ($CC00-$CFE7) and the KERNAL's ($0400-$07E7) with fill_memory, turns bitmap mode off ($D011 bit 5) and the sprites off, and shows the text screen (text_screen).
The credits (credits), with lines of up to 250 characters ($03F6).
SOUNDFX (file 3) over MDRIVER at $BA00; start_effects points the driver at SOUNDFX's own sounds and starts sound 0, silence.
Every resource slot's file number to $FF ($6E13-$6E2B, all 25), so that each loads when first wanted.
Clears $8300-$8AFF and $4900-$64FF, the game's variables and party, then the clock ($49C6-$49CC) once more.

The starting values: area script 0 waiting to load in slot 8 ($6E1B = $80), $6D78 = 1, some twenty of the resident's variables to 0 (among them the restart count $6DDD and the party cursor $6D7B), no close-up head ($6DE1 = $FF) and $6E6D = 16.

Loads ITEMS (file 0, $7B00-$82FF), ITEMNAMES (1, $6F00-$797B, over the packed title), DUNGEON2 (4, $7A00) and COMBAT3 (9, $7AC0), then ANIMATE00 into resource slot 11 ($8400), and puts the KERNAL's interrupt back.

Every party slot's combat icon (default_icons), then more starting values: portraits and monster pictures on ($49FF = $81), square 0,0 of map 0 in a 3D area ($49C0, $49C1, $49C5, $49E6 = 1), the menu's wait at 250 ($1379), white highlights ($03F8) and green text ($0286, $6E34). Then the menu bar PLAY GAME DEMO (play_menu).
Waits for the choice: wait_menu_choice, then menu_key, which moves the highlight or chooses. When the wait runs out the choice is 1, DEMO. The choice goes to $6DA0.

PLAY GAME: clears the menu bar, wants disk side 3 ($6E12), message speed 2 ($49FC), then the code-word question (code_wheel). Slot 3 must load SECSET02 again over the runes ($6E16 = $82), and the next module is GEN ($6E11 = 0), party creation.

DEMO: frames the screen and clears the main window, puts area script $1E in slot 8 to load ($6E1B = $9E, the file ECL1E), sets $6DDD to 1 and the message speed to 2, and makes DUNGEON the next module ($6E11 = 1).

Waits for a key or the joystick: up to 250 times 256 rounds of a 200-pass delay loop while nothing is pressed (read_input gives $FF and the joystick reads $1F). Returns carry set with the key in A, the wait back at 250, when something is; carry clear when the time runs out.

Loads INIT's file X (0-9): its name from init_name_lo/hi and init_file_lengths into load_file's name ($301C/$301E), its address from init_load_lo/hi. On an error asks for the disk (disk_prompt) and tries again.
INIT's ten file names, run together with no ends: ITEMS, ITEMNAMES, CHARSET, SOUNDFX, DUNGEON2, TITLEPG, MUSIC, SPR.TP, MDRIVER, COMBAT3.
ITEMNAMES, file 1's name.
CHARSET, file 2's name.
SOUNDFX, file 3's name.
DUNGEON2, file 4's name.
TITLEPG, file 5's name.
MUSIC, file 6's name.
SPR.TP, file 7's name.
MDRIVER, file 8's name.
COMBAT3, file 9's name.
Each name's length in init_file_names, by file number: 5, 9, 7, 7, 8, 7, 5, 6, 7, 7.

Where each file loads, low bytes, by file number: ITEMS $7B00, ITEMNAMES $6F00, CHARSET $6500, SOUNDFX $BA00, DUNGEON2 $7A00, TITLEPG $6F00, MUSIC $C400, SPR.TP $C000, MDRIVER $BA00, COMBAT3 $7AC0. load_file takes these, not the addresses in the files' own first two bytes.
The load addresses' high bytes.
Where each name starts in init_file_names, low bytes.
The names' high bytes, all $0A.
Nothing calls this. It changes every character code of $40 or more on screen rows 24 to 0 into a space (cursor_row_address for each row), leaving letters, digits and punctuation.
Copies X pages and A bytes from ($FB) to ($FD) with all 64 KB as RAM (all_ram), so that it can write under the I/O area; through $A7-$AA. Gives the ROMs and I/O back ($3AB1) at the end.
Gives each of the eight party slots' combat icons ($4BE0, 36 bytes each) default_icon's 36 bytes.
Steps the icon pointer ($07/$08) on.

The combat icon INIT gives every party slot: the ready pose's nine character codes ($20 $A0 $20, $86 $87 $88, $06 $07 $08), the action pose's ($20 $A0 $20, $89 $8A $8B, $06 $10 $11), then their eighteen colours, all blue ($0E: 6, plus 8 for multicolour) but the top middle cell of each pose, the head, which is yellow ($0F).
A counter: default_icons counts the eight slots down in it, and credits keeps its place in credits_script here.
Unpacks TITLEPG from $6F00 to $DC00 on, with all 64 KB as RAM (all_ram): the picture's colours, then its bitmap at $E000.

Each control byte: $00-$7F copies that many bytes (unpack_copy; 0 copies 256), $80-$FE repeats the next byte its low seven bits' times (unpack_run; $80 repeats it 256 times), and $FF ends, giving the ROMs and I/O back ($3AB1).
Reads the next packed byte from ($FB) and steps on; A and the flags are the byte's.
Steps the packed pointer ($FB/$FC) on.
A run: the next byte, stored A AND $7F times (put_unpacked).
Stores A at ($FD) and steps that pointer on.
A copy: the next A bytes, each stored as it comes.

Nothing calls this. With all RAM showing (all_ram) it asks fill_memory to fill from $FFFF up to $DC00 with 0. fill_memory counts upwards, so as written it would clear $FFFF and then go on from $0000, through the zero page and the program itself; a clear of the title's memory, $DC00-$FFFF, would have the two addresses the other way round.

The title. A grey border ($0C) and the screen off ($D011 bit 4) while TITLEPG (file 5) loads and unpacks (unpack_title) and SPR.TP (7) and MUSIC (6) load. Then VIC bank 3 ($DD00), colours at $DC00 and bitmap at $E000 ($D018), hires ($D016 bit 4 clear), the screen on, and six sprites from the tables at $0D11: 0 to 2 red and behind the picture ($D01B = 7), filling the TSR logo, 3 to 5 white sparkles. Clears the blank sprite at $C1C0, starts the sparkles out of step, turns bitmap mode on, starts the interrupt (game_irq) and tune 12, the title tune.
Until a key comes or the tune has been silent for 256 passes (tune_silent): each pass moves the sparkles on (sparkle_loop). The joystick does not end the title.

For each sparkle, 2 to 0 ($0D49): with a chance of 15 in 256 (random below 15) it moves on one frame (sparkle_frame, through the sixteen of sparkle_frames), written to its sprite pointer ($DFFB + the sparkle). At the last frame ($FF) the sprite takes the blank picture (pointer 7) and moves to a random place, X 74 to 293 and Y 80 to 219, with its bit in $D010 set or cleared.
Stops the tune (start_tune with 0, silence), waits (delay 0) and puts the KERNAL's interrupt back.

The six sprites' X positions, by sprite number: 156, 174 and 197 for the logo's three pieces, 0 for the sparkles until they move. Each of these four tables has a seventh byte that is never read, as the loop starts at sprite 5.
The sprites' Y positions: 52 ($34) for the logo, 0 for the sparkles.
The sprites' colours: red (2) for the logo, white (1) for the sparkles.
The sprites' first pictures, as pointers into bank 3 ($C000 plus 64 times the pointer): 0, 1 and 2 for the logo, 3 (the whole star) for each sparkle.
Where each sparkle starts in sparkle_frames: 0, 5 and 10, so that the three twinkle out of step.
A sparkle's frames, as sprite pointers: 6 (a dot), 5, 4, 3 (the whole star) and back to 6 over fifteen frames, then $FF, which hides and moves it.
Each sparkle's place in sparkle_frames.
Each sparkle's bit cleared, for an AND with $D010 (sprites 3, 4 and 5).
Each sparkle's bit, for an OR with $D010 when its X is 256 or more.
The sparkle sparkle_loop is on, 2 to 0.
Points the driver's data at MUSIC ($C400 in $BA0E/$BA0F) and starts tune A (sound_start, through $BA03): 12 the title tune, 0 silence.
Points the driver, SOUNDFX by now, at its own sounds ($BD7B) and starts sound A (0, silence).
Moves the cursor to the next row at the window's left edge ($03F2) and prints INIT's message X (print_init_message).
Prints INIT's message X at the cursor: its address from init_message_lo/hi into $07/$08, then print_string.
Message 0, the heading of the credits: "CREDITS".
Message 1, a line of the credits (credits_script): "SCENARIO CREATED BY:".
Message 2, a line of the credits (credits_script): "TSR, INC.".
Message 3, a line of the credits (credits_script): "JIM WARD,".
Message 4, a line of the credits (credits_script): "DAVID COOK, STEVE WINTER,".
Message 5, a line of the credits (credits_script): "MIKE BREAULT".
Message 6, a line of the credits (credits_script): "GAME CREATED BY:".
Message 7, a line of the credits (credits_script): "SSI SPECIAL PROJECTS".
Message 8, a line of the credits (credits_script): "PROGRAMMERS:".
Message 9, a line of the credits (credits_script): "ARTISTS:".
Message 10, a line of the credits (credits_script): "KEITH BRORS".
Message 11, a line of the credits (credits_script): "TOM WAHL".
Message 12, a line of the credits (credits_script): "BRAD MYERS".
Message 13, a line of the credits (credits_script): "DARLA MARASCO".
Message 14, a line of the credits (credits_script): "SUSAN HALBLEIB".
Message 15, a line of the credits (credits_script): "DEVELOPERS:".
Message 16, a line of the credits (credits_script): "FRED BUTTS".
Message 17, a line of the credits (credits_script): "GEORGE MAC DONALD".
Message 18, a line of the credits (credits_script): "MAURICE MOLYNEAUX".
Message 19, a line of the credits (credits_script): "VICTOR PENMAN".
Message 20, a line of the credits (credits_script): "VINCE REYNOLDS".
Message 21, a line of the credits (credits_script): "PAUL MURRAY".
Message 22, a line of the credits (credits_script): "RUSS BROWN".
Message 23, a line of the credits (credits_script): "PROJECT MANAGER:".
Message 24, a line of the credits (credits_script): "DAVE SHELLEY".
Message 25, a line of the credits (credits_script): "CHUCK KROEGEL".
Message 26, a line of the credits (credits_script): "TESTERS:".
Message 27, a line of the credits (credits_script): "JOEL BILLINGS, STEVE SALYER,".
Message 28, a line of the credits (credits_script): "JAMES KUCERA,ROBERT DALY,JOHN BRUNING".
Message 29, the first line of the code-word question: "USE THE TRANSLATION WHEEL TO DECIPHER".
Message 30, the question's second line: "THE CODE WORD.".
Message 31, the line after the path, saying which way to read the wheel: "READ FROM THE INSIDE TO THE OUTSIDE.".
Message 32, over the Espruar rune: "MATCH THE ESPRUAR RUNE (OUTER RING)".
Message 33, over the Dethek rune: "WITH THE DETHEK RUNE (INNER RING)".
Message 34, over the path: "AND READ THE CODE WORD UNDER THE PATH:".
The end of message 34 (msg_and_read_the, $0FDB), across the edge of the memory map at $1000.
Message 35, path 0, a dotted line: "......".
Message 36, path 1, dashes and dots: "..-..-..".
Message 37, path 2, a solid line: "------".
Message 38, the prompt before the typed word: "INPUT THE CODE WORD:".
Message 39, the answer to a wrong code word: "WRONG !!!".

The twelve code words, seven bytes each with the zero that ends them: BEWARE, COPPER, DRAGON, EFREET, FRIEND, JUNGLE, KNIGHT, NOTNOW, TEMPLE, VULCAN, WYVERN, ZOMBIE. code_wheel compares all seven bytes, so the typed line must be the six letters and nothing more.
The addresses of INIT's forty messages, low bytes: 0 to 28 for the credits, 29 to 39 for the code-word question.
The messages' addresses, high bytes.
draw_box for the four bytes whose address is in A (low) and X (high), then character 0, the corner square, at the box's four corners in yellow (box_corners), and the text colour back ($6E34).
Puts character 0 at the box's left and right columns ($48F2, $48F4) on row A.

The credits: clears the main window and the menu bar, a black border, the frame round the screen ($4835) and a box across rows 2 to 7 (credits_box_edges), then the lines of credits_script, typed out with the text delay at 5 ($03FC), and the delay off again.
The box round the credits' heading: columns 0 to 39, rows 2 to 7.

The credits as a script for credits: a byte below $80 prints that message, $FE goes to the next row, $C0-$FD sets the column (the low six bits), $80-$BF the colour (the low three bits), and $FF ends. CREDITS in white at column 16; then SCENARIO CREATED BY: in green and TSR, INC. in yellow, the designers in cyan; GAME CREATED BY: SSI SPECIAL PROJECTS; programmers and artists, developers, the project manager and the testers in two columns, headings yellow and names cyan.

Counts silent_count down when none of the three streams has a wait left and none of the three voices a gate time ($BD35/$BD42, $BD37/$BD44, $BD39/$BD46), with interrupts off while it reads them. Returns zero when the count comes back round to 0, after 256 silent passes.

The code-word question. Loads SECSET10, the rune characters, into slot 3 ($6500) and copies $600 bytes of it to $D200 (characters $40-$FF); clears and frames the window; picks a word (code_word, 0-11) and a path (code_path, 0-2) at random. Prints USE THE TRANSLATION WHEEL TO DECIPHER / THE CODE WORD., MATCH THE ESPRUAR RUNE (OUTER RING) with the Espruar rune at column 10 below it (two characters, espruar_runes), WITH THE DETHEK RUNE (INNER RING) with the Dethek rune (dethek_runes), AND READ THE CODE WORD UNDER THE PATH: with the path's line (message 35, 36 or 37), READ FROM THE INSIDE TO THE OUTSIDE., then INPUT THE CODE WORD: and reads up to ten characters (input_line). It returns when all seven bytes match the word's entry in code_words.
The Espruar rune: two characters from espruar_runes at the word times six plus the path times two, plus $3F.
The Dethek rune: one character from dethek_runes at the word times three plus the path, plus $3F.
The comparison: the word's seven bytes at $1039 plus seven times code_word, against the typed line at $9700.

A wrong word: WRONG !!!, a pause (delay 8); the first time a new question (code_wheel again, a new word and path at random). The second time the game stops at $12F4 for good, a jump to itself that only a reset ends.
The jump to itself after a second wrong code word.
The Espruar rune shown for each word and path, two characters side by side, each code less $3F (the rune characters from $40 on): six bytes for each word, a pair for each of its three paths.
The right-hand characters of the Espruar runes, every other byte from here.
The Dethek rune shown for each word and path, one character less $3F: three bytes for each word, one for each path.
The menu bar PLAY GAME DEMO for menu_bar: two items, an empty heading, then each item's text.
The two items' texts: PLAY GAME, then DEMO with a space before it.
tune_silent's count of silent passes, from 0 round to 0.
The code word asked for, 0 to 11 (random_to 11), its place in code_words.
The path asked for, 0 to 2: dots, dashes and dots, or a solid line (messages 35 to 37). It picks the runes shown; the word to type does not depend on it.
wait_menu_choice's inner count, 256 rounds.
wait_menu_choice's outer count, from 250 down.
Set after the first wrong code word; with it set the next wrong word hangs the game.

CHARSET, the game's font for character codes $00-$3F, eight bytes each: a corner square at $00, the letters A to Z at $01-$1A, a solid block at $1C (input_line's cursor), line pieces for frames at $1E and $1F, then punctuation and the digits from $20. copy_block puts it at $D000, the start of the text screen's characters, where print_string's codes ($41-$5A ANDed with $BF) find the letters.

TITLEPG, the title picture packed by runs (unpack_title): a control byte $00-$7F copies that many bytes, $80-$FE repeats the next byte, $FF ends. It unpacks to 9,216 bytes from $DC00 to $FFFF. These first 167 bytes give $DC00-$DFFF: the colours of the picture's 1,000 cells, ink in the high four bits and paper in the low, and 24 bytes after them, the last eight where the sprite pointers go ($DFF8), which title_screen then sets.
From here the bitmap at $E000, 320 bytes to a row of characters. Rows 0 to 2: the grey outline of the TSR logo, which the red sprites fill in from behind, between two red lines.
Still the packed rows 1 and 2, the logo and its lines. The resident's print_item_name ($39D8) reads from $7000, the second page of ITEMNAMES, which INIT loads over this picture.
Rows 3 to 6: PRESENTS, An Official Advanced Dungeons & Dragons, COMPUTER PRODUCT.
Rows 7 to 11: the top of the blue ring and the words POOL OF.
Rows 12 to 17: RADIANCE and the bottom of the ring.
Rows 18 to 21: A FORGOTTEN REALMS and Fantasy Role-Playing Epic, Vol. I.
Rows 22 to 24, the two copyright lines, then zeros on to $FFFF; the $FF that ends the picture is at $7E5A.

MDRIVER, the title tune's player, loaded here by INIT before SOUNDFX takes its place; the entry for each interrupt, called by irq ($3BEA). Its code is SOUNDFX's, apart from the addresses of the instruments. Plays nothing while a tune is being started ($BD79) or with the volume ($BA06, written to $D418) at 0; otherwise brings in its zero page and steps the three streams (sound_voice, $BA33), then puts its zero page away.
sound_start's jump: INIT starts a tune here with A, its number in the table at the data's base (start_tune, $0D4A), and stops it with 0.
The SID volume the driver writes to $D418 each interrupt (0 stops it playing); 12 in this snapshot.
The volume sound_start copies to $BA06 when it starts a tune.

The driver's copy of its zero page, $B2-$B9: the three streams' read pointers ($B2/$B3, $B4/$B5, $B6/$B7) and the data's base ($B8/$B9 here at $BA0E/$BA0F), which start_tune sets to MUSIC at $C400. sound_zp_in ($BC59) and sound_zp_out ($BC64) swap them with the zero page.
The data's base, low byte, in the zero page copy: INIT writes it before starting a tune ($00 for MUSIC, $7B for SOUNDFX's sounds at $BD7B).
The data's base, high byte ($C4 for MUSIC).
The body of sound_play, for each interrupt.

Steps stream X and the SID voice of the same number (0, 2 or 4): nothing when the stream's wait ($BD35) and the voice's gate time ($BD42) are both over. Adds the voice's frequency slide ($BD65) to its frequency ($BD53) and its pulse sweep ($BD6B) to its pulse width ($BD59), counts the gate time down and clears the gate bit when it reaches the release point ($BD48), counts the stream's wait down and at 0 reads the stream's next commands (sound_commands). Then writes the voice's frequency, pulse width, envelope and control to its SID registers ($D400 + the offset at $BC78).

Reads a stream's commands until one makes it wait. A byte $00-$0F sets field n under the stream's number (its offset in $BC7D) to the next byte, or the next two from field 10 on, and $00, the wait, ends the step (a wait of 0 ends the stream). $40+n is a repeat: two bytes, high first, give a target from the data's base, and the counter n bytes on from the stream's wait is counted down: the stream jumps back while it is not yet 0, and a counter at 0 jumps always. $80+ is a note (sound_note, $BB0E). The title tune is notes from start to end, then $00 $00.

Starts a note for stream X. Bits 3-6 of the note byte pick its length from note_lengths ($BD7B, plus the stream's length base, $BD36), which becomes the stream's wait; bits 0-2 its instrument, plus one. The next byte is its pitch: $3F a rest; otherwise a SID voice is taken ($BD7A): from the third voice down, the first free one (its gate time, $BD42, and the wait of the stream of its number both 0) that holds this instrument already, or else the lowest free one, or the stream's own voice when none is free. The instrument's nine bytes are loaded into it from $BD8B unless it holds the instrument already ($BD4E), the frequency set from the note table ($BC8D, pitch plus transposition), the voice's gate time set to the note's length and the gate opened. A pitch with bit 7 set means another note follows in the same step, on another voice when one is free: a chord.

The voice search: $BD7A starts as the stream's own voice, then voices 4, 2 and 0 are tried in turn. When none is free the stream's own voice takes the note, so the branch at $BB57 always goes on and the jump at $BB59 is never taken.
A new instrument for the voice: its nine bytes, from instruments ($BD8B) at the offset instrument_offsets gives.
The note's frequency: the pitch's low six bits plus the voice's transposition, times two, into the note table; the gate time is the stream's new wait.
Pitch bit 7: read the next note byte and start that note too.
Reads the next byte of stream X into A and $BD77 and steps its pointer ($B2,X) on.

Starts tune A: sets the volume ($BA07 to $BA06), takes the tune's entry from the table at the data's base (six bytes each: the three streams' offsets, 0 for an unused stream) and for each stream used points it there, clears all the stream's fields and gives it a wait of 2. $BD79 keeps sound_play out while it works.
Copies the driver's saved zero page ($BA08) into $B2-$B9.
Copies $B2-$B9 back to the driver's save ($BA08).
Where each of the eight instruments starts in instruments ($BD8B): nine bytes apart, 0 to 63.
Each voice's first SID register, by number 0, 2 or 4: $D400, $D407, $D40E.

For each of the sixteen fields a command can set, its offset from the wait ($BD35): 0 the wait, 1 the length base, 6 and 7 and 12 the repeat counters, 13 the gate time, 18 the control, 19 the release point, 24 the transposition, 25 the instrument, then the two-byte ones: 30 frequency, 36 pulse width, 42 envelope, 48 frequency slide, 54 pulse sweep, 60 pulse width to start each note with.
84 SID frequencies, low byte first, seven octaves of semitones from 536 (about 32 Hz) upwards, read by sound_note; the same table as SOUNDFX's.
The high bytes of the note frequencies, every other byte from here (note_frequencies, $BC8D).

The fields, eleven rows of six bytes with a pair for each number 0, 2 and 4 (the row and offset in field_offsets, $BC7D): waits and length bases, repeat counters, gate times, control and release points, transposition and instrument, frequency, pulse width, envelope, frequency slide, pulse sweep, starting pulse width. The wait, length base and repeat counters are a stream's; the rest are the SID voice's of that number, which a note writes into whichever voice it takes and a stream's own commands write under the stream's number. The first stream's wait, $BD35, is one of the six bytes tune_silent ($11C1) reads to know the tune has ended.
Each stream's length base, added to a note's length number before note_lengths is read (the wait's partner in the first row of sound_fields); the title tune leaves it at 0.
The second stream's wait, one of the six bytes tune_silent reads; its length base follows.
The third stream's wait and length base; the title tune runs on this stream. Then the repeat counters at offsets 6 and 7 for each stream ($BD3B-$BD40) and the first stream's third counter ($BD41).
Each voice's gate time: a note sets it to the note's length in the voice it takes (sound_note), and sound_voice counts it down; the voice's gate closes when it reaches the release point ($BD48).
The second voice's gate time, which tune_silent reads.
The third voice's gate time, which tune_silent reads.
Each stream's control: the SID waveform and gate bits written to the voice's control register.
Each voice's release point, the gate time at which sound_voice closes the gate.
Each stream's transposition, added to a note's pitch.
The instrument each voice holds, so a note on the same instrument does not load it again.
Each stream's frequency, low byte; its high byte is at $BD54.
Each stream's frequency, high byte.
Each stream's pulse width, low byte; its high byte is at $BD5A.
Each stream's pulse width, high byte.
Each stream's attack and decay, written to the voice's $D405.
Each stream's sustain and release, written to the voice's $D406.
Each stream's frequency slide, low byte, added to the frequency each step.
Each stream's frequency slide, high byte.
Each stream's pulse sweep, low byte, added to the pulse width each step.
Each stream's pulse sweep, high byte.
The pulse width a stream's notes start with, low byte.
The pulse width a stream's notes start with, high byte.
The last byte read from a stream (sound_byte).
A working number: the instrument, a counter's number, or six times the tune's number.
Set while sound_start works, so that sound_play leaves the streams alone.
The SID voice a note takes (sound_note).

The note lengths in interrupts (sixtieths of a second), by a note byte's bits 3-6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72 and 96 at numbers 3, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14 and 15, and 0 at the others. A quarter note of 24 is 0.4 seconds, so the tune runs at 150 beats a minute.

The eight instruments, nine bytes each: control, transposition, release point, attack and decay, sustain and release, starting pulse width (two bytes) and pulse sweep (two bytes). 1, 2, 5 and 6 are pulse waves, 3 and 4 sawtooth, 7 triangle, and 8 a pulse an octave up (transposition 12).
An instrument's second byte, its transposition, read by sound_note.
An instrument's third byte, its release point.
An instrument's fourth byte, its attack and decay.
An instrument's fifth byte, its sustain and release.
An instrument's sixth byte, the low byte of its starting pulse width.
An instrument's seventh byte, the high byte of its starting pulse width.
An instrument's eighth byte, the low byte of its pulse sweep.
An instrument's ninth byte, the high byte of its pulse sweep; the table runs on to $BDD2, the end of MDRIVER.

SPR.TP's seven sprites, 64 bytes each, at pointers 0 to 6 of bank 3: 0 to 2 ($C000, $C040, $C080) the red that fills the TSR logo, in three pieces side by side. Each sprite's 64th byte, which the VIC never shows, holds the colour the game gives it: 2 for the logo, 1 for the sparkles.
Still sprite 0. The resident's gdrive_call ($407B) calls $C003, GDRIVE's draw_view, which loads here in the modules that draw the 3D view.
Sprite 1, the logo's middle piece.
Sprite 2, the logo's right-hand piece.

The sparkle's four sizes, pointers 3 to 6: the whole four-pointed star, a smaller star, a small cross and a single dot ($C180). Pointer 7, at $C1C0 just past SPR.TP, is the blank sprite title_screen clears.

MUSIC, the data MDRIVER plays at the title. Its table has twenty entries, six bytes each: the offsets from $C400 of the entry's three streams, 0 for none. Entries 0 to 11 are SOUNDFX's twelve sounds, their streams copied here; 12 is the title tune, and 13 to 19 start the same tune at its later sections. INIT only starts entry 12, and entry 0 to stop it.

Entries 12 to 19: each points its first two streams at sound 0's silence ($C56F) and its third at the tune, from its start (title_tune, $C609) or from one of its seven later sections (title_tune_2 to title_tune_8).

SOUNDFX's sound streams, copied: the same commands as SOUNDFX's at $BDC3-$BF53, with each repeat's target 48 bytes further on, because this table is eight entries longer than SOUNDFX's. Nothing plays them from here.
Sound 0's stream, which the tune entries give their first two streams: the gate closed, then a wait of 0, which ends the stream.

The title tune, the third stream of entry 12: notes from start to end, two bytes each, the length and instrument then the pitch (bit 7 of the pitch for another note in the same step, a chord), and $00 $00 at $CF59. The tune lasts 5,976 interrupts, about a minute and 40 seconds at 60 a second, in eight sections, 1,100 notes and 92 rests. Section 1, from the start: 19.6 seconds, 180 notes and 42 rests on instruments 1, 4 and 5.
Section 2, where entry 13 starts, 19.6 seconds in: 9.7 seconds, 148 notes on instruments 1 and 3.
Section 3, entry 14, 29.3 seconds in: 17.3 seconds, 217 notes and 26 rests on instruments 1, 3 and 6.
Section 4, entry 15, 46.6 seconds in: 6.8 seconds, 88 notes and 6 rests on instruments 1, 2 and 3.
Section 5, entry 16, 53.4 seconds in: 14.2 seconds, 126 notes and 4 rests on instruments 2, 5 and 6.
Section 6, entry 17, 67.6 seconds in: 9.7 seconds, 107 notes and 6 rests on instruments 3, 4 and 8.
Section 7, entry 18, 77.3 seconds in: 9.5 seconds, 91 notes on instruments 1, 2, 3, 7 and 8.
Section 8, entry 19, 86.8 seconds in: about 12.8 seconds to the end, 143 notes and 8 rests on instruments 1 to 5.
The tune's end: field 0, the wait, set to 0, so the stream reads no more; when its last notes have died away tune_silent starts counting.
